subject.title: fix(scripts): warn when postinstall detects running gateway with stale module imports

question: Should OpenClaw add an npm postinstall loopback probe plus OPENCLAW_DISABLE_POSTINSTALL_RESTART_WARNING as a partial stale-gateway mitigation, or keep warning/recovery in the update/runtime layer only?
rationale: The code defects from the prior review are fixed, but choosing package-install probing and a new env suppression surface is an install/upgrade product boundary decision rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Accept postinstall advisory mitigation
options.body: Land this PR after maintainer review as a low-risk warning-only mitigation, while leaving #92241 open for the complete stale-import recovery decision.

options.title: Prefer update/runtime recovery only
options.body: Pause this PR and focus on #99330 or a runtime stale-import detector so warnings live where OpenClaw already owns update and gateway lifecycle state.

options.title: Reject warning-only package probing
options.body: Close this PR if maintainers do not want npm lifecycle scripts to probe local services even for advisory output.

recommendation.title: Accept postinstall advisory mitigation
recommendation.body: Land this PR after maintainer review as a low-risk warning-only mitigation, while leaving #92241 open for the complete stale-import recovery decision.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest current history signal across postinstall, service metadata, and update lifecycle code touched by this product-boundary choice.
